grammar.title: Track what happens each time
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + たびに; event noun + のたびに.
grammar.explanation: Links an event to a response on each occurrence. Yamamoto checks the inspection record whenever a service update arrives. Compare a recurring event with a single completed Monday update. Emotional response is possible, not required; the expression is not an arbitrary clock interval.
grammar.example: 更新のたびに、点検の記録を確認します。
grammar.translation: Each time there is an update, I check the inspection record.

examples.ja: {更新|こうしん}のたびに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: Each time there is an update, I check the inspection record.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}むたびに、{新|あたら}しいことに{気|き}づきます。
examples.en: Each time I read the same sentence, I notice something new.

examples.ja: {予定|よてい}が{変|か}わるたびに、{参加者|さんかしゃ}に{伝|つた}えます。
examples.en: Whenever the schedule changes, I tell the participants.

grammar.mistake: Use 更新のたびに, not 更新たびに. A dictionary verb precedes たびに even when describing past repeated occasions; tense of the main clause can be past. One observation is not proof of a recurring habit.

grammar.title: A whole span, an event within it, and full progress
grammar.formation: Interval: attributive verb/い-adjective; noun の; な-adjective な + 間(に). Full progress: verb ている or noun の + 最中に; predicate 最中だ.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 intervals. 間 can frame activity continuing throughout a span; 間に places an event or completion inside it. 最中に emphasises being right in the middle of an action, often with an interruption. It need not always mean interruption. Another action taking some time inside the span is allowed; avoid a false instantaneous-only rule.
grammar.example: 説明会の間、私はずっとメモを取っていました。
grammar.translation: I took notes throughout the information session.

examples.ja: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、{私|わたし}はずっとメモを{取|と}っていました。
examples.en: I took notes throughout the information session.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{間|あいだ}に、{要約|ようやく}を{読|よ}み{終|お}えました。
examples.en: During the break, I finished reading the summary.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}している{最中|さいちゅう}に、{着信|ちゃくしん}がありました。
examples.en: An incoming call arrived right in the middle of the explanation.

grammar.mistake: Use ている最中, not dictionary-form 説明する最中 in the construction taught here. Name a construction when testing attachment; no claim that all near-synonyms are unacceptable.

grammar.title: Use a window before it changes; notice gradual change
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary/ている/ない + うちに; い-adjective + うちに; な-adjective な; noun の.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve unit 2: act while a condition persists or before it changes. Negative 忘れないうちに means before forgetting. In another use, a change gradually occurs while doing something repeatedly. うちに does not always express a deliberate opportunity; read whether the main clause is a planned act or an emerging change.
grammar.example: 内容を忘れないうちに、要約を書きました。
grammar.translation: I wrote the summary before I forgot the content.

examples.ja: {内容|ないよう}を{忘|わす}れないうちに、{要約|ようやく}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote the summary before I forgot the content.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かなうちに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}みましょう。
examples.en: Let us read the inspection record while it is quiet.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}んでいるうちに、{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かるようになりました。
examples.en: As I continued reading the same sentence, I came to understand its meaning.

grammar.mistake: 静かなうちに uses な; noun + の. Do not translate 忘れないうちに as after forgetting. The gradual-change use need not imply an intentional deadline.

grammar.title: A recurring tendency is not an identity
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem/noun + がち; predicate がちだ/です; modifier がちな or がちの where idiomatic.
grammar.explanation: Describe a propensity, usually an unwanted one. Kenta reports repeatedly leaving things out when hurried, rather than just one Monday event. がち is often negative but not absolutely restricted to negative events. Dates and words such as よく clarify how often something happens. Its focus can overlap with 気味, so attachment tasks name the target.
grammar.example: 急ぐと、説明を省略しがちです。
grammar.translation: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.

examples.ja: {急|いそ}ぐと、{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しがちです。
examples.en: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.

examples.ja: {大切|たいせつ}なことを{忘|わす}れがちなので、メモを{取|と}ります。
examples.en: I tend to forget important things, so I take notes.

examples.ja: {欠席|けっせき}がちな{時期|じき}がありました。
examples.en: There was a period when I was often absent.

grammar.mistake: 省略します→省略しがち, not 省略するがち. Look for repeated events in the context. がち versus 気味 is not a universally exclusive choice.

grammar.title: A slight state or sign in the speaker’s account
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem/noun + 気味 (suffix read ぎみ); predicate 気味だ/です; common modifier 気味の and adverb 気味に.
grammar.explanation: Describes a mild sign, state or inclination. Kenta says he felt a little tired yesterday. That differs in focus from his repeated omission habit, but 気味 is not universally temporary and がち not universally permanent. Use the surrounding dates, repetition words and speaker’s description to follow the intended meaning.
grammar.example: 昨日は疲れ気味でした。
grammar.translation: I felt a little tired yesterday.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}でした。
examples.en: I felt a little tired yesterday.

examples.ja: {作業|さぎょう}は{遅|おく}れ{気味|ぎみ}ですが、{四時|よじ}までに{終|お}わります。
examples.en: The work is running a little behind, but it will finish by four.

examples.ja: {寝不足|ねぶそく}{気味|ぎみ}だったと、{本人|ほんにん}が{話|はな}しました。
examples.en: The person said they were somewhat short on sleep.

grammar.mistake: 疲れます→疲れ気味, not 疲れる気味. Read the suffix ぎみ; standalone 気味 has different readings/uses. Choose the named attachment, and retain self-report attribution.

dialogues.title: What happened during the session
dialogues.scene: Tuesday morning, Bao and Yamamoto review Monday’s information session, which began at four as announced. They distinguish ongoing note-taking from one phone call handled by a colleague.

lines.meaning: Yesterday’s information session began at four as scheduled. Let us review the record this morning.

lines.romaji: Hai. Chakushin e no ōtō wa betsu no hito ga tantō shita node, watashi wa memo o tsuzukeraremashita.

lines.meaning: Yes. Before I forgot the content, I wrote that the factors behind the malfunction were under investigation.

dialogues.title: A repeated habit and yesterday’s tiredness
dialogues.scene: Tuesday after lunch, Kenta and Misaki compare a repeated communication habit with Kenta’s description of yesterday. Bao suggests a concrete way to keep the summary complete.

lines.meaning: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations. Last week, for three consecutive days, I left one thing out each time.

lines.romaji: Sore wa kurikaesu kuse no hanashi da ne. Kinō no kibun dake no hanashi to wa chigau n da.
lines.meaning: That is about a repeated habit, right? It differs from only describing yesterday’s state.

lines.meaning: Yes. Yesterday I was short on sleep and felt a little tired. I felt fatigue, but I will write that separately from last week’s habit.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto-san. Agree to write the summary before you forget the content.
exercises.line: {忘|わす}れないうちに、{要約|ようやく}を{書|か}いてください。
options: はい。{今|いま}、{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だと{書|か}きます。
{全部|ぜんぶ}{忘|わす}れた{後|あと}で、{初|はじ}めて{書|か}きます。
{要因|よういん}は{不明|ふめい}ですが、{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったと{書|か}きます。
exercises.explain: The first acts now before forgetting and retains the stated investigation status.

exercises.meaning: I took notes throughout the information session.
tiles: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、
メモを{取|と}っていました。
exercises.explain: 間 and ずっと frame the continuing note-taking across the session.

exercises.prompt: What repeated pattern does Kenta describe?
options: Leaving one explanation out each day for three consecutive days last week
Missing the four-o’clock session yesterday
Forgetting everything just once on Tuesday
exercises.explain: 先週は三日連続で、毎回一つずつ describes the recurrence.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta say about yesterday?
options: He was short on sleep and felt somewhat tired
He did not attend the session
He omitted one explanation every hour
exercises.explain: 寝不足 and 疲れ気味 report yesterday’s state, distinct from last week’s habit.

options: Yes, he attended at four despite feeling tired
No, he was absent
The scene never states whether he attended
exercises.explain: He explicitly says 参加した and 欠席はしなかった.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 省略します with the named suffix がち, to express a tendency to omit explanations.
exercises.line: {急|いそ}ぐと、{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}＿＿がちです。
options: し
する
した
exercises.explain: The ます-stem of 省略します is 省略し; remove ます.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 疲れます with the named suffix 気味 (ぎみ), to describe mild tiredness.
exercises.line: {昨日|きのう}は{疲|つか}れ＿＿でした。
options: {気味|ぎみ}
る{気味|ぎみ}
ます{気味|ぎみ}
exercises.explain: 疲れ is the stem; 疲れ気味 describes being somewhat tired.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta. Suggest a concrete check before he sends the summary.
exercises.line: {説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しがちなんだ。
options: {送|おく}る{前|まえ}に、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}と{要約|ようやく}を{比|くら}べよう。
{昨日|きのう}は{欠席|けっせき}したから、{記録|きろく}はないね。
{確認|かくにん}の{手間|てま}は{必|かなら}ず{省|はぶ}こう。
exercises.explain: The first suggests comparing the record and summary; the second contradicts his attendance and the third removes the needed check.

exercises.meaning: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.
tiles: {省略|しょうりゃく}しがちです。
exercises.explain: The condition precedes the recurring tendency; the verb stem attaches to がち.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: Which event belongs to Monday rather than Tuesday?
options: The four-o’clock information session
Kenta’s lunchtime account of last week
Writing the diary’s Tuesday heading
exercises.explain: Yesterday refers to Monday in the Tuesday diary.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: Which statement describes repeated actions last week?
options: Kenta omitted one explanation on each of three consecutive days
Bao finished the summary during one break
A single call arrived during Monday’s explanation
exercises.explain: 三日連続 and 一つずつ establish recurrence; the other events happen once.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: What new practice has been decided?
options: Check the inspection record each time a summary is sent
Skip the checking effort when tired
State that all causes are now known
exercises.explain: 送るたびに…確認することにした connects each send to the decided check.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a time-span or habit line from your own clip. Mark the time clues and whether it describes one event, repetition, or a slight state.
